sources.title: Warp pricing
sources.locator: Warp Terminal and agents plans, checked 7 November 2026
sources.finding: Free, Build, Max, Business and custom Enterprise plans distinguish included usage, collaboration and customer-supplied inference.

sources.title: Platform usage
sources.locator: How platform usage is measured; when charges apply
sources.finding: Cloud runs incur platform usage even on self-hosted workers. Eligible dollar-billed plans charge $3 per agent-hour; inference and hosted compute are separate.

sources.title: Cloud agents
sources.finding: Cloud-agent documentation separates factories from standalone runs and lists local/cloud handoff, API access and configured worker execution.

sources.title: Agent harnesses
sources.finding: Factories and standalone runs support Warp Agent, Claude Code and Codex. The current page makes plan eligibility conditional instead of a fixed Build minimum.

sources.title: Cloud agent session sharing
sources.locator: What it enables; inactive sessions; fork to local
sources.finding: Authorized users can inspect and follow up remote runs while the VM remains active; after shutdown a conversation can be forked locally.

sources.title: Factory inbox
sources.finding: A personal queue gathers questions, spec/PR reviews, blocked and failed items for tasks the user started.

sources.title: Warp Factories overview
sources.finding: The official docs label Factories Early Access, separate from standalone cloud-agent availability.

sources.title: Oz web app for cloud agents
sources.finding: Browser/mobile app creates runs, agents, skills, schedules, environments and integrations. Runs include status, creator, source, outputs, cost and parent/child inspection.

sources.title: Oz CLI reference
sources.locator: Run; API key; Schedules; Agent configs
sources.finding: Oz CLI runs native agents in cloud or on the current host and manages runs, schedules, environments, MCP, skills, secrets and identity using Warp authentication.

sources.title: How Warp Factories work
sources.finding: Factory work items retain identity across triage/spec/implementation/review. Foreman dispatches specialized agents, returns revisions to existing conversations and hands PRs to humans. Spec gates are instruction policy and merges require repository controls.

sources.title: Multi-agent orchestration
sources.finding: Native parent/child orchestration is one level deep, supports mixed Warp/Claude/Codex harnesses, durable per-agent inboxes, lifecycle events and wake-on-followup. Cloud-local shares filesystem; other cloud children have their own environments.

sources.title: Configuring harness authentication
sources.finding: Managed-secret Claude Code/Codex cloud setup uses funded provider API credentials. Local Codex ChatGPT sign-in is explicitly different. Factory auth secrets must be team scoped; ad hoc personal runs may use personal secrets.

sources.title: Self-hosting overview
sources.finding: Enterprise workers support Docker/Kubernetes/Direct/Command execution on customer compute. Warp retains the control plane, operational metadata and billing. Transcript/artifact buckets are independently configurable.

sources.title: Unmanaged execution
sources.finding: oz agent run executes on the current CI, Kubernetes, VM or dev host on macOS/Linux/Windows. Repeatable --share flags grant team/user view or edit access.

sources.title: Direct backend Git worktrees
sources.finding: Direct tasks can use per-run worktrees and branches through configured setup/teardown hooks. These share host processes/network/Git metadata and are not OS sandboxes.

sources.title: Configuring cloud agent environments
sources.finding: Standalone environments configure multiple authorized GitHub repos, Docker images and setup commands. Guided setup recommends tooling. Runs default non-root when possible but may retain root if non-root setup fails.

sources.title: Self-hosted worker reference
sources.finding: max-concurrent-tasks defaults unlimited and queues excess work when capped. One-shot Direct forces one task; completion-idle settings and Kubernetes resource/timeouts are configurable.

sources.title: Cloud agent session sharing
sources.finding: Cloud sessions expose commands, logs, plans and artifacts, permit followups while the environment is active, and fork conversations locally after shutdown; code branches may require manual clone.

sources.title: Factory inbox
sources.finding: Personal Inbox includes questions, spec approvals, PR reviews and blocked/failed items only for tasks started by that person. Items auto-clear or can be resolved/undone and filtered.

sources.title: Managing factory permissions
sources.finding: Enterprise Factory user/Editor roles control run versus configuration rights, with Admin management and factory-specific overrides. Non-Enterprise members are Editors; role does not grant merge or spec approval authority.

sources.title: MCP servers for cloud agents
sources.finding: Cloud agents use stdio or remote MCP plus managed OAuth installations; factory-wide versus per-agent grants are separate. Connected Slack/Linear/Jira integration tools need no separate MCP installation.

sources.title: Factory MCP for coding agents
sources.finding: Hosted Factory MCP can send/list/search/get tasks, retrieve conversation, message foreman and hand work back with task identity. OAuth or agent key has full principal permissions, no read-only/per-factory scope.

sources.title: Factory dashboard
sources.finding: Dashboard exposes run timeline/cost/subagents, PR cycle time and estimated cost per PR including children. Warp-managed definition edits validate and commit; agent-proposed definitions use spec-review inbox with request-changes or approve/merge.

sources.title: Warp product and services license agreement
sources.finding: Hosted Warp products use a limited proprietary service license with redistribution/reverse-engineering restrictions. Vendor support uses Pacific business hours with reasonable one-business-day response efforts.

sources.title: Warp Terminal
sources.finding: Warp app has macOS, Windows and Linux downloads and is a client for standalone cloud runs.

sources.title: Cloud agents quickstart
sources.finding: The desktop Warp app opens standalone cloud-agent conversations, configures environments and inspects retained run records.

sources.title: Scheduled Agents
sources.finding: Scheduled agents execute server-side cron workflows, each with fresh context. CLI/web edit, pause and delete controls are documented; no environment yields a bare sandbox. CLI-created schedules run as creator unless changed in web app.

sources.title: Agent harnesses
sources.finding: Factory and standalone cloud runs use skills and project Rules, with each harness retaining its own tool/context behavior. Config and auth are selected per factory agent or ad hoc run.

sources.title: Warp Trust Center
sources.finding: Vendor states SOC2 TypeII and provides Enterprise reports on request. Scope lists security, availability, confidentiality and processing integrity; no report was inspected.

sources.title: Warp Factories: Infrastructure for Software Factories
sources.locator: Product name; introductory description; early-access CTA
sources.finding: The current factory offering is branded Warp Factories and described as infrastructure for software factories. Current page still offers request early access. This does not establish that all standalone Oz workflows were renamed or discontinued.

sources.title: Transitioning from Oz to Warp Factories
sources.locator: Opening paragraph; Current status table; Existing web app workflows
sources.finding: Factories is the web experience for team workflows; existing standalone workflows continue using Oz web app, Oz CLI, SDKs and API references. New software factories use platform.warp.dev. The guide describes adoption/migration rather than an explicit complete product rename.

sources.title: Build the factory. Let it run. Go kayaking.
sources.finding: The October 3 vendor post uses Warp Factories and describes transition from early access toward general availability. A statement of transition is not an exact GA launch date or proof that current access gates ended.

sources.title: Oz Cloud Agent Platform: Every agent at your command
sources.finding: The /oz page retains the Oz Cloud Agent Platform title and links standalone automation to oz.warp.dev, while global navigation promotes Warp Factories. This retained standalone naming limits any inferred blanket Oz rename.

sources.title: Cloud agent session sharing
sources.finding: Shared cloud agent runs execute on remote virtual machines, whose code/config changes, commands, logs and outputs can be reviewed through Warp or the browser. Idle environments can shut down.

sources.title: Handoff from local to cloud
sources.finding: Local-to-cloud handoff transfers an active conversation and workspace snapshot so a long-running task can continue without keeping the laptop awake.
